transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I'm mostly here because... well, my wife and my director at work kind of insisted. 

They think I'm doing too much. I guess I just... I can't seem to stop launching new projects. Things like drafting up new work plans, packing my schedule with IT certifications, upgrading the whole home network... even just sending out messages to old contacts. 

I just keep going. I guess it gets pretty intense, and I sort of... blow past normal limits. I don't really notice until my wife or my director has to step in and tell me to stop. So... that's why I'm here.
Have you noticed needing less sleep lately, or feeling rested with just a few hours of sleep?

I guess... yeah. There have been runs where I only sleep maybe three hours. I'll just wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m. 

I don't really feel tired, though. It just feels like... I don't know, like I've been handed bonus time to get things done.

latest_inference.note: The patient's report of needing less sleep and increased activity supports a manic episode, aligning with Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic without psychotic features. Other candidates were ruled out based on the presentation not fitting criteria for Major Depressive Disorder (F32.1), Bipolar II Disorder (F31.6), or Adjustment Disorder (F43.22).

inference_history.note: The patient describes persistent over-involvement in activities, launching new projects, and ignoring limits, which suggests possible mania or hypomania. This leads to consideration of bipolar disorders (F30.1, F31.1, F31.6), as well as the possibility of a major depressive disorder with associated stress (F32.1, F43.22). No information yet rules out or confirms specific disorders, so the list remains broad.
